newsitem.title: PERU: Foreign investment in Peru up $166.65 mln in Sept.
newsitem.headline: Foreign investment in Peru up $166.65 mln in Sept.

text.p: Direct foreign investment in Peru rose $166.65 million in September to a total registered stock of $5.888 billion, the government's National Commission of Foreign Investment and Technology (CONITE) said Thursday.
The CONITE, which could not give comparative figures for August 1995, started registering foreign investment in 1988.
The organisation added that total foreign investment in shares traded on the Lima Stock Exchange -- which is monitored separately -- was $3.368 billion at the end of August.

The main investor country in Peru in recent years is Spain with $2.36 billion of the total stock. This is due mainly to purchases in local privatizations by Telefonica de Espana and Banco Bilbao Vizcaya.

Other heavy investors in Peru are the United Kingdom with $1.06 billion of the total, the United States with $840.2 million, the Netherlands with $304.1 million, Panama with $220.4 million, and Chile with $215.3 million.
